s1.syndrome_frame: Progressive orbital swelling with vision deterioration and proptosis
salient_findings: Left fronto-orbital swelling of 10 years’ duration
Progressive deterioration of vision in the left eye
Proptosis with inferior and medial displacement of the left globe
Heterogeneous enhancing mass in the left orbital roof on MRI
key_facts: 35-year-old woman
Left fronto-orbital swelling for 10 years
Progressive vision deterioration in the left eye over 1.5 years
Proptosis became more pronounced over the past month
Left globe displaced inferiorly and medially
No history of endocrine abnormalities
Heterogeneous enhancing mass in the left orbital roof on MRI
Expansive lytic bony lesion involving the superior and lateral walls of the orbit on CT scan

shortlist.label: Orbital meningioma
shortlist.why_kept: Heterogeneous enhancing mass in the left orbital roof on MRI, consistent with meningioma

shortlist.label: Fibrous dysplasia
shortlist.why_kept: Expansive lytic bony lesion involving the superior and lateral walls of the orbit on CT scan, consistent with fibrous dysplasia

shortlist.label: Sphenoid wing meningioma
shortlist.why_kept: Location and imaging findings suggestive of sphenoid wing involvement, a common site for meningiomas

shortlist.label: Fronto-orbital osteoma
shortlist.why_kept: Expansive lytic bony lesion and location in the fronto-orbital region, consistent with osteoma

shortlist.label: Plexiform neurofibroma
shortlist.why_kept: Long-standing orbital swelling and vision deterioration, with potential for neurofibromatosis type 1 association

raw.rationale: The presence of a heterogeneous enhancing mass in the left orbital roof on MRI, along with the progressive deterioration of vision and proptosis, is most consistent with an orbital meningioma, which is known to cause such symptoms due to its potential to compress and displace orbital structures.

rejected.label: Fibrous dysplasia
rejected.why: While fibrous dysplasia can cause orbital lesions, it typically presents with ground-glass appearance on imaging and may not fully explain the rapid progression of symptoms.

rejected.label: Sphenoid wing meningioma
rejected.why: Although this could explain some findings, the primary location described is the orbital roof, which is more suggestive of an orbital meningioma.

rejected.label: Fronto-orbital osteoma
rejected.why: Osteomas are typically benign, slow-growing, and might not fully account for the rapid progression of vision loss and proptosis.

rejected.label: Plexiform neurofibroma
rejected.why: This condition is associated with neurofibromatosis type 1 and typically presents with multiple neurofibromas and other systemic manifestations, which are not mentioned in the vignette.
